name: AWS EC2 Trn1 / Trn2 (AWS Trainium and Trainium2)
region: us-east-1 on-demand; Capacity Blocks across us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-2, eu-north-1
price_basis: per Trainium chip-hour. trn1.32xlarge = 16x Trainium, on-demand $21.50/instance-hr / 16 = $1.3438; Capacity Block $9.532/16 = $0.596 (AWS's own per-accelerator figure). trn1n.32xlarge = $24.78/16 = $1.5488. trn2.48xlarge = 16x Trainium2, NO on-demand rate published in the us-east-1 price list - Capacity Block only, $35.7608/16 = $2.235; trn2.3xlarge = 1x Trainium2 at $2.235. Fetched 2026-10-03.
notes: Trainium1 at $1.34/chip-hour is the cheapest on-demand accelerator hour any hyperscaler publishes in this slice, and 4x cheaper again via Capacity Block at $0.596 - but that is an apples-to-oranges comparison against GPU pricing and should not be read as 'Trainium is cheap'. You pay in Portability: workloads run through AWS Neuron (PyTorch and JAX native), not CUDA, and every kernel, quantization format and engine elsewhere in this repo assumes CUDA unless it lists a TPU or Neuron path. trn2 has NO on-demand rate published at all in the price list fetched, the same capacity signal as the p5 $0.00 sentinel - you get it via Capacity Block reservation. Trainium2 spec from the product page: 96GB HBM per chip; 1.5TB and 46TB/s per 16-chip instance; trn2u.48xlarge joins a 64-chip UltraServer over NeuronLink. AWS claims 30-40% better price-performance than GPU-based P5e and P5en - a vendor claim, and price-performance is not price. No published commitment or savings-plan discount for trn1/trn2; Capacity Block is the discount channel. Anthropic's Project Rainier runs on Trainium2, which is evidence the software path is real, not that it is easy.
